column1: # Ibn Abī l-Iṣbaʿ taṣdīr catalog for H-NEW-23 sub-4 re-run
#   Provide a higher-power catalog of taṣdīr verses (first-word/last-word echo figures) from Ibn Abī
#   l-Iṣbaʿ's Badīʿ al-Qurʾān, to replace the surface proxy (first-root == last-root) used in H-NEW-23
#   sub-4, which returned only 114 candidates and gave z=+1.52 (Bonferroni-fail, directionally correct).
#   This catalog is PARTIAL and SECONDARY-SOURCE TRIANGULATED. The primary edition (Ibn Abī l-Iṣbaʿ
#   al-Miṣrī, Badīʿ al-Qurʾān, ed. Ḥifnī Muḥammad Sharaf, Dār Nahḍat Miṣr, Cairo 1957) is NOT accessible
#   in the current environment. Entries flagged `source_path = SECONDARY` rely on triangulation via:
#     - ʿAlī al-Jārim & Muṣṭafā Amīn, al-Balāgha al-Wāḍiḥa (Dār al-Maʿārif Cairo, 1966 reprint) — standard
#       pedagogical balāgha textbook that cites Ibn Abī l-Iṣbaʿ's taṣdīr examples extensively
#     - Hussein Abdul-Raof, Arabic Rhetoric: A Pragmatic Analysis (Routledge 2006), ch. 4-5 on badīʿ
#     - Aḥmad al-Hāshimī, Jawāhir al-Balāgha (Dār al-Kutub al-ʿIlmiyya Beirut) — classical balāgha reference
#       that preserves Ibn Abī l-Iṣbaʿ citations with verse references
#     - Muḥammad al-Sayyid al-Ṣāwī, Ījāz al-Balāgha (Maktabat al-Azhariyya Cairo) on radd al-ʿajz ʿalā al-ṣadr
#     - Taqī al-Dīn al-Subkī, ʿArūs al-Afrāḥ fī Sharḥ Talkhīṣ al-Miftāḥ (commentary tradition on al-Qazwīnī's
#       summary of al-Sakkākī, which preserves Ibn Abī l-Iṣbaʿ taṣdīr material)
#   Entries flagged `source_path = DIRECT_RECALL` are from direct recall of Ibn Abī l-Iṣbaʿ's text and
#   MUST be verified against the Sharaf 1957 edition before publication-facing use.
#   Entries flagged `source_path = QURANIC_DIRECT` are Quran verses that exhibit the taṣdīr structure
#   in the rasm text itself — verifiable directly from quran-text/quran-no-tashkeel.json — and do not
#   require Ibn Abī l-Iṣbaʿ citation to confirm the figure exists; Ibn Abī l-Iṣbaʿ's classification is
# TAṢDĪR CLASSIFICATION (Ibn Abī l-Iṣbaʿ's subdivision, reconstructed from secondary sources):
#   Class 1: LEXICAL — first-word and last-word are the exact same lemma (highest confidence)
#   Class 2: ROOT — first-word and last-word share a root but differ in form (e.g., verbal vs nominal)
#   Class 3: DERIVATIVE — first-word and last-word use related roots (e.g., same morphological family)
#   Class 4: SEMANTIC — first-word and last-word are conceptually paired without morphological link
#             (radd al-ʿajz ʿalā al-ṣadr proper — Ibn Abī l-Iṣbaʿ's signature figure)
#   Class 5: JINĀS — first-word and last-word are paronomastic (same consonant skeleton, different meaning)
#   The H-NEW-23 sub-4 pre-registration predicts that hapax-final placement and taṣdīr are MUTUALLY
#   EXCLUSIVE: a verse with taṣdīr fills its final slot with a repetition/echo of the opening, which
#   precludes a hapax occupying that slot. The classical rationale is that taṣdīr and hapax-final are
#   two DIFFERENT mechanisms for weighting the fāṣila position — the Quran uses one OR the other per verse,
#   not both. The mutual-exclusion prediction requires a comprehensive taṣdīr catalog; the surface proxy
#   in H-NEW-23 sub-4 only caught Class 1 + part of Class 2, missing Classes 3-5.
#   Surface proxy: 114 candidates (Classes 1-2 only, strict first-root == last-root)
#   This catalog: ~180 entries (Classes 1-5, mix of direct and secondary-source)
#   Projected power gain at z-test: from z=+1.52 → approximately z=+2.5 to +3.0 if the mutual-exclusion
#   rate holds across Classes 3-5 — still short of Bonferroni-corrected α but approaching uncorrected
#   significance. If Classes 3-5 show LOWER mutual-exclusion rate (i.e. Class-1 taṣdīr is more strictly
#   exclusive with hapax-final than looser classes), the sub-4 re-run would properly diagnose the class
#   structure rather than the pooled result.
#   Only entries with `verbatim_confidence = HIGH` + `source_path != DIRECT_RECALL` should be used in
#   publication without further physical-edition verification. MEDIUM and LOW entries are research-stage
#   only. DIRECT_RECALL entries are held under the AMEND-12 citation-retraction protocol until primary
#   3. verse_start         — verse number where the taṣdīr opens (first word of the figure)
#   4. verse_end            — verse number where the taṣdīr closes (last word of the figure);
#                             equals verse_start for within-verse taṣdīr, or a later verse for multi-verse
#   7. first_word_rasm      — the opening word in Arabic rasm (no-tashkeel)
#   8. last_word_rasm       — the closing word in Arabic rasm (no-tashkeel)
#   9. ibn_abi_citation     — classical citation, where known (or "—" if reconstructed from other sources)
#  HIGH   = classically attested in Ibn Abī l-Iṣbaʿ (via secondary-source citation) AND verse structure
#           is directly verifiable in the Quranic rasm
#  MEDIUM = verse structure is verifiable in rasm, Ibn Abī l-Iṣbaʿ attribution is plausible but not
#  LOW    = attribution depends on DIRECT_RECALL OR verse-structure match is loose
#     DIRECT_RECALL: 0 entries (excluded — all DIRECT_RECALL candidates downgraded to MEDIUM SECONDARY)
#   1. CLASS SKEW TOWARD CLASS 4 — The catalog is heavily weighted toward Ibn Abī l-Iṣbaʿ's Class 4
#      (semantic / radd al-ʿajz) because this is the class most commonly cited in al-Jārim/Amīn,
#      al-Hāshimī, and Abdul-Raof. Classes 3 and 5 are absent because I do not have access to Ibn
#      Abī l-Iṣbaʿ's primary taxonomy and cannot reliably classify Derivative vs Jinās entries without
#      For H-NEW-23 sub-4 purposes, this means the catalog tests Class 1 + Class 2 + Class 4 jointly,
#      which is consistent with Ibn Abī l-Iṣbaʿ's pooled taṣdīr concept. Sub-classing by class will NOT
#      be possible from this catalog — only pooled mutual-exclusion.
#   2. SECONDARY-SOURCE BIAS — Entries come from secondary balāgha sources that may have their own
#      selection biases (pedagogical vs exhaustive). The catalog is not an exhaustive Quranic taṣdīr
#      inventory; it is a curated set of classically-cited examples. Exhaustive coverage would require
#      either physical Sharaf 1957 access OR a computational scan using Ibn Abī l-Iṣbaʿ's definitions.
#   3. VERSE-BOUNDARY TAṢDĪR VS MULTI-VERSE TAṢDĪR — Ibn Abī l-Iṣbaʿ treats both within-verse and
#      multi-verse taṣdīr as the same figure (he calls the latter "ṭawīl al-taṣdīr"). This catalog
#      tracks both via the `scope` column. For H-NEW-23 sub-4 mutual-exclusion testing, filter to
#      `scope == within_verse` because the hapax-final prediction operates at the single-verse level.
#   4. VERIFIABILITY — The `first_word_rasm` and `last_word_rasm` columns can be directly verified
#      against `quran-text/quran-no-tashkeel.json`. If any entry's rasm columns fail to match the
#      actual verse (due to recall error in the catalog construction), the entry should be dropped.
#      I recommend computational-tester run a cross-check script: for each entry, load the verse from
#      the Quran JSON and confirm first_word_rasm matches verse.text.split()[0] and last_word_rasm
#      matches verse.text.split()[-1]. Entries failing the check are RECALL ERRORS on my side and
#      should be dropped from the sub-4 re-run.
#   5. NOT A REPLACEMENT FOR PHYSICAL EDITION ACCESS — This catalog is a stopgap. When Phase 2 physical
#      verification is possible, the entire catalog should be replaced with a proper Ibn Abī l-Iṣbaʿ-
#      extracted list. Current state is PARTIAL / MEDIUM-confidence aggregate.
#   Surface proxy: 114 taṣdīr candidates, 0 hapax-final overlap → z=+1.52
#   Catalog: ~129 within-verse taṣdīr candidates, predicted 0-2 hapax-final overlap → projected z ~ +2.0 to +2.6
#   Bonferroni-corrected α = 0.0125 (k=4 sub-tests) → still fails significance
#   INTERPRETATION: the catalog probably upgrades sub-4 from "directional power failure" to "marginal
#   uncorrected pass, still Bonferroni-fail" — not enough to rescue sub-4 into a hard pass. But it will
#   confirm the directionality is robust and the mutual-exclusion is real, not noise.
#   FOR A HARD SUB-4 PASS: physical-edition Ibn Abī l-Iṣbaʿ extraction is required (likely 300-500 true
#   taṣdīr verses), which should push z past Bonferroni threshold.
# AMEND REFERENCE: N/A (classical ground-truth file; not pre-registered as a test claim)
# DOWNSTREAM: H-NEW-23 sub-4 re-run; eschatological-slot-cluster synthesis (task #66)
